A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Muon convergence-analysis work. All 24 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Algorithms, mathematical results and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 optimizer experiments, MNIST gradient/Hessian diagnostics and synthetic quadratic experiments in Figures 1–3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports quadratic experiments, data-spectrum and regression analyses, revised MNIST experiments and Shakespeare language-model training in Figures 1–5 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same gradient estimation, momentum, SVD orthogonalization and parameter updates. Newton–Schulz approximation remains mentioned, although its detailed appendix is removed. The additional GPT experiment does not introduce a new proposed optimizer.

E1.justification: V2 adds MNIST-based linear regression with original and random labels, Gaussian-input controls, Shakespeare embedding-spectrum analysis and character-level language-model training. CIFAR-10 classifier training is removed, while CIFAR-10 remains in a new data-spectrum analysis. MNIST MLP and synthetic quadratic coverage remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds GD with Nesterov momentum to the linear-model comparisons in Figure 2 and evaluates AdamW against Muon in Figure 4. V1's five-way CIFAR-10 comparison is removed. GD versus Muon remains the comparator pairing in the matched quadratic and MLP experiments.

E3.justification: The retained MNIST MLP experiment changes its stated subset from 60 to 120 samples. New protocols include 1,000-sample MSE experiments with 10- and 100-dimensional outputs and six-layer GPT training for 1,000 steps with batch size 64. The GPT setup uses scaled, weight-decayed Muon for non-embedding matrices and AdamW for remaining parameters.

E4.justification: V2 adds real-data versus Gaussian controls and output-dimension comparisons to test when rank structure helps or hurts Muon. It also extends curvature/gradient diagnostics to GPT matrices and adds CIFAR-10 and text-spectrum analyses. V1's momentum and SVD-versus-Newton–Schulz ablations are removed.

E5.justification: V1 reports five random seeds and means with one standard deviation for Figure 1(a). That experiment and its uncertainty reporting disappear in v2, which provides no corresponding repeated-run uncertainty reporting for the new experiments. The 10,000-sample quadratic ratio histogram remains.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports Muon's advantage on MNIST-derived regression data and disadvantage on Gaussian controls, with comparison ratios 1.57, 3.52, 0.0122 and 0.0232 in Figure 2. GPT results are added, CIFAR-10 ablation results are removed, and MNIST MLP curves change under the revised sample count. The original quadratic plots are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds the Hessian/smoothness equivalence proof in Lemma A.3 and a stochastic analysis without uniform Lipschitz smoothness in Appendix B.4. It sharpens Kronecker-based bounds and revises the star-convex weighted-curvature bound. Existing uniform-smoothness results are largely reorganized. New mathematical inconsistencies include the unsupported nuclear-norm bound by D_op in Section 4.1.1 and the missing 1/B factor in Equation (4) relative to Equation (3).

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion now emphasize low-rank Hessians and omit the earlier explicit approximate-block-diagonality claim, although that analysis remains in Section 4.2.1. The central contributions remain convergence guarantees under different assumptions and conditions for Muon's advantage over GD.

C2.justification: V2 develops a new explanation linking concentrated real-data spectra to Hessian structure and interprets the Gaussian controls and output-dimension effects as boundaries on Muon's advantage. It explicitly describes the Lambda-smoothness assumption as restrictive. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit small-network limitation and the discussion supporting practical SVD/Newton–Schulz equivalence.

D1.justification: V2 adds GPT architecture/training details, nanoGPT and Shakespeare source links, and RoBERTa text-embedding construction instructions. Reported GPU hardware changes from H100 to RTX 6000 Ada. It removes the Newton–Schulz coefficients and iteration-count documentation, along with the retained MNIST experiment's explicit learning-rate grid and selected rate of 0.1.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against recent Muon theory and variants, including Pethick et al., Davis and Drusvyatskiy, Ma et al., Crawshaw et al., and momentum variance-reduction work. These additions discuss overlapping explanations and guarantees. Adam and ReLoRA bibliography updates concern existing works rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: Section 4 is reorganized from nonconvex/star-convex cases into Frobenius, spectral and nonuniform smoothness regimes. Several appendix results move into the main text, contribution bullets disappear, and related-work and interpretation passages are extensively rewritten. V2 also introduces widespread incorrect 'Theorem' references to assumptions, definitions and lemmas.

P2.justification: V2 adds the multi-panel regression/spectrum Figure 2, GPT Figure 4 and appendix spectrum Figure 5, while removing v1's CIFAR-10 and Newton–Schulz figures. The unchanged quadratic plots move from Figure 3 to Figure 1. MLP plots are replaced and relocated, its architecture table is renumbered, and a GPT hyperparameter table replaces the CIFAR-10 architecture table.

improvement.justification: The Gaussian controls, GPT experiment and additional proofs strengthen explanatory evidence and coverage. However, v2 removes practical optimizer ablations, five-seed uncertainty reporting and useful reproducibility details, while introducing norm-comparison and Hessian-normalization errors in Sections 4.1.1 and 4.2.1. For a paper centered on convergence theory, these unresolved mathematical issues and lost validation make the net quality improvement uncertain.
